title: Swimming League Splashes Back With All-Star Match
summary:
The International Swimming League, known as the ISL, is coming back after a break of more than five years. British swimming star Adam Ramsay-Peaty is leading the way.

The ISL is a fast, team-based swimming league that first started in 2019. It stopped after 2021 because of the war in Ukraine and its effect on the league's backer, Ukrainian businessman Konstantin Grigorishin. It is back now, starting with a big All-Star Match on 19 December at the Aquatics Centre in London.

Ramsay-Peaty, a three-time Olympic champion, will swim for the Commonwealth team, alongside South African swimmer Pieter Coetzee. Nine-time Olympic champion Caeleb Dressel was among the first names picked for the United States team.

Four teams will race in London: Commonwealth, United States, Europe and Intercontinental. In all, 96 swimmers will race in 46 races packed into just two hours.

Ramsay-Peaty said athletes should support the league's return, calling it a nice rejuvenation.

The organisers say they have learned from past money troubles and will take things slowly, hoping the match leads to a full return.
why_it_matters: Team swimming shows that working together matters in sport, just like teamwork matters when you play games or swim with friends.
